enriched_description: Small leporid mammal measuring 30-40 cm body length with compact rounded body. Fur dense and soft in greyish-brown coloration providing cryptic camouflage. Ears moderately long (5-7 cm) with dark tips. Tail short and fluffy with distinctive white underside visible during flight. Hind legs elongated and muscular adapted for saltatorial locomotion. Forelegs shorter with clawed digits for digging. Eyes large and laterally positioned providing wide field of view. Nose twitching with split upper lip. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, dense fur insulation, and four-chambered heart. Host for Ixodes tick species.

Swift leporid mammal measuring 45-70 cm body length with elongated body and powerful hind limbs. Fur dense in brown, gray, or seasonal white coloration. Ears exceptionally long (10-15 cm) with black tips. Hind legs massively elongated with muscular thighs enabling rapid leaping at speeds exceeding 60 km/h. Forelegs shorter. Tail short. Young born precocial with full fur coat and open eyes. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Timid behavior with cryptic resting posture. Larger than rabbit with longer ears and legs.

Domestic rabbit breed with exceptionally long silky white fur measuring 7-12 cm in length. Body compact and rounded weighing 2-5 kg. Fur dense, fine, and wool-like requiring regular grooming. Ears long and tufted with fur. Eyes pink or blue in albino strains. Hind legs muscular but concealed beneath abundant coat. Tail small and fur-covered. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Bred specifically for fiber production. Requires shearing or plucking every 90 days.

Small rodent measuring 5-15 cm body length with stocky compact body. Fur dense and short in golden, brown, black, or white coloration. Head broad with prominent cheek pouches extending to shoulders for food storage. Eyes small and dark. Ears rounded and relatively large. Tail very short and stubby. Legs short with clawed digits; hind feet slightly elongated. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Nocturnal burrowing behavior. Cheek pouches lined with elastic mucosa for transport of food to burrow.

Large rodent measuring 60-90 cm body length with stocky robust body. Fur interspersed with sharp erectile quills (modified hairs) measuring 5-30 cm. Quills keratinous with barbed tips that detach easily upon contact. Coloration dark brown to black with contrasting white or yellow quill bands. Head small with short ears. Eyes and nose small. Legs short and stout with strong claws for climbing. Tail short and quill-covered. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Defensive quill erection mechanism controlled by arrector pili muscles.

Exceptionally large tree squirrel measuring 45-70 cm total length with bushy tail comprising half body length. Fur grizzled gray-brown dorsally with orange-brown underparts. Tail long and bushy with mixed gray, brown, and black hairs. Ears small and rounded without tufts. Eyes large and dark. Forelegs shorter than hind legs with sharp curved claws for climbing. Body robust and muscular. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Arboreal with agile climbing ability. Constructs leaf nests (dreys) in tree branches.

Stocky rodent measuring 40-70 cm body length with coarse dense fur in brown, gray, or reddish coloration. Body robust and barrel-shaped weighing 3-7 kg. Head broad with short rounded ears. Eyes small and dark. Legs short and powerful with strong curved claws for digging. Tail short and bushy. Fur thick providing insulation for hibernation. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Burrowing behavior with extensive underground tunnel systems. Hibernates in winter with lowered metabolic rate and body temperature.

Large semiaquatic rodent measuring 70-100 cm body length weighing 11-30 kg. Fur dense waterproof double coat with dark brown coloration. Tail broad, flat, paddle-shaped and scaly measuring 20-30 cm. Hind feet large and webbed for swimming. Forelegs shorter with dexterous claws for manipulation. Head broad with small eyes and ears. Incisors large, orange-pigmented, and continuously growing for gnawing wood. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Constructs complex dams and underwater lodges from branches and mud.

Stout-bodied rodent measuring 20-25 cm body length weighing 0.7-1.2 kg. Fur short and smooth in variable coloration including white, brown, black, or multicolored patterns. Body compact and cylindrical with no visible tail. Head blunt with short rounded ears. Eyes large and prominent. Legs short with four toes on forefeet and three on hind feet. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Domesticated cavy widely used in research. Social animal with vocal communication including wheeking and purring.

Equine mammal measuring 140-170 cm at withers with athletic build. Coat uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coloration with no black points. Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen). Head elongated with large expressive eyes and mobile ears. Neck arched and muscular. Body deep-chested with strong back. Legs long and slender with single hoof per foot. Tail long with flowing hair. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse body hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Color variant of horse distinguished by reddish-brown coat.
